meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

examples.text: Мы сюда зачем прилетели? Я сразу сказал: с ним ничего не получится.
examples.trans: What did we even fly out here for? I said from the start: nothing will come of it with him.
Why did you even come here? Empty-handed!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А ну-ка, дай посмотрю! Внимание, ребята!
examples.trans: Hold on, let me have a look! Attention, everyone!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'bye', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our, ours', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'head chef, executive chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

examples.text: Шеф-повар решит, подходите ли вы ресторану.
examples.trans: The head chef will decide whether you suit the restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дыхать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to rest, relax', paired with 'отдохнуть'.

examples.trans: Everything is great, get some rest!
In the summer we vacation by the sea.

examples.text: Всё отлично, отдыхай! Сегодня выходные, всё круто!
examples.trans: Everything is great, get some rest! It is the weekend today, everything is cool!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

лечиться.gloss: to undergo treatment, to be treated

meanings.en: to undergo treatment, to be treated
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to undergo treatment, to be treated', paired with 'вылечиться'.

examples.trans: He is being treated in the hospital.
This condition is treated with medication.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean'.

examples.trans: Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'чего').

examples.text: Ты знаешь, что я хочу. Мне терять нечего.
examples.trans: You know what I want. I have nothing to lose.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, вам больше нечего сказать?
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, do you have nothing more to say?
There was nothing left to ruin there!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not a (single); neither... nor', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'down, fluff (ни пуха = good luck)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Alright, best of luck to you all.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый пух.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new down.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'feather' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A beautiful feather fell from the bird.
It turned out like that because of feathers.

examples.text: Оказалось, что у него очень густые перья.
examples.trans: It turned out that it has very thick feathers.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'щаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to communicate, to talk with'.

examples.trans: I am not allowed to talk with you.

examples.text: Мне с вами вообще общаться нельзя. Всего доброго.
examples.trans: I'm not allowed to talk to you at all. Good day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'quit, threw', paired with 'бросать'.

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

examples.text: Ну ладно, брось! Мы только поедим.
examples.trans: Oh come on, stop it! We'll only eat.

examples.text: А он тут, соседи сверху бросили. Уже месяц висит на улице!
examples.trans: It's right here, the upstairs neighbours threw it. It's been hanging outside for a month already!
